content:
zoe: Quick pulse from the all-hands Q&A  a few customers asked for plain-language rules about credit buckets, quotas, and bursting. Can we capture the canonical lines here so Sales/Support can use them?
matt: Sure. Short rules: credits = prepaid consumption units on Hosted; quotas = enforced windows (requests/min, tokens/day) that apply to any org or route; dedicated customers buy reserved throughput (pools) with their own burst windows.
nora: Couple of nuance Qs that came up live: 1) Are hosted credits "use-it-or-lose-it" at month end? 2) Can Hosted traffic burst above quotas if the cluster has slack? 3) Do Dedicated pools ever get preemption rights over Hosted?
eli: Answers: 1) Default self-serve credits expire at the end of the billing/credit period (no automatic carry-forward). Enterprise contracts can opt into different handling. 2) Hosted allows controlled short bursts when there is spare capacity; those bursts are gated by per-tier ceilings and a global safety buffer. If headroom disappears we fallback or throttle rather than abruptly killing requests. 3) Dedicated pools are allocated isolation and priority within their configured placement; we do not preempt running Hosted prompts, but allocation bias favors reserved pools when scheduling new work.
eli: Sales wants concrete, clearly-labeled sample numbers for the cheat-sheet (marked "illustrative"). Can we pick a set thats different from previous examples so slides feel fresh?
matt: Example (illustrative): Trial org: 75k tokens/day, burst cap 15k tokens/30s; Startup/Growth: 1,000,000 tokens/day, burst cap 200k tokens/1min; Enterprise: negotiated. We'll flag these as subject to change.
nora: Customers also asked about "grace buffer" behavior  what happens when they hit quota mid-request?
matt: We never drop an in-flight response due to quota checks. If a request would exceed the window we finish the current run, then apply soft-degradation on subsequent requests: shorter completions, fallback model, or temporary 429s depending on settings. That guarantees no sudden truncation.
nora: Is there an API customers can call to show remaining credits/quotas in their product?
eli: Yes  public endpoint planned: GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/usage. It will return: credit_balance, active_rate_limits, token_windows (day/hour/min), and per-route thresholds. We'll include an SDK helper to emit a short human summary like "13% of monthly credits left".
zoe: tiny nit: can the API also surface a small "explainable reason" code when a request is throttled (so customers can show a callout in-app)?
matt: Good point. We'll include a throttling_reason field with codes like "RATE_LIMIT", "POOL_EXHAUSTION", or "FALLBACK_MODEL". Docs PR will list exact codes.
nora: Billing Q: are prepaid hosted credits refundable if unused?
billing-bot: Standard self-serve credits are non-refundable. Any refund/rollover arrangements are contractual and handled by Finance for enterprise deals.
nora: Ops Q: what monitoring will alert customers or support before they hit limits?
ops-bot: Dashboard alerts: org-token usage thresholds at 70% and 95% by default; configurable for enterprise. New panel shows 24h burn rate and projected exhaustion time.
nora: Can Docs prepare a short cheat-sheet (single page) we can attach to demo decks: includes the short canonical blurb, the sample numbers, the burst semantics, the API example + sample JSON response, and the no-in-flight-preempt note?
docs-bot: Creating DOCS ticket now: "docs: pricing cheat-sheet + usage API sample" assigned to matt/nora. Will include sample JSON and code snippet in python/js.
eli: Thanks everyone  please ping here when the PR lands so Support can add to the playbook.
